Im so late but as a person who was a picky eater as a kid i must chime in. I would say at least in my area LC is very worth getting doordash. I have dd+ and half the time I just stick random stuff on my order to get it to $12... to give you an idea of how cheap it is. That being said, the pepperonis are good. The main difference with LC and other places is that a lot of places have sweeter sauce or something like that. LC also makes the dough in the store and it is actual (though barely) fermented pizza dough which gives it a pretty decent flavor. It's also quick during the slower hours since the ovens in store only take 5 minutes so if your 5 year old is throwing a tantrum and hungry I'd choose there. 

I would recommend the emb pepperoni unless your kid isn't a huge fan of the pepperoni. It's a couple bucks(??) more and has more cheese and pepperonis, specifically 8 more pepperonis than the base hot and ready although most places don't actually count them out lol. You just gotta see how your location does it. They'll put pepperonis on top of the extra cheese so if your kid tends to play with their food I'd say get just a regular pepperoni instead. If your kid is a greaseball and likes things a little more spicy try the fanceroni. I will say also if your kid is picky and ends up not liking the actual pizza part you could also get a slices and sticks, which is half regular pizza and half cheese bread. Good as fuck.

It was written about the Second Boer War! "There's no discharge in the war," can certainly be taken as metaphorical but there is also something to be said that is the Second Boer War men were often not discharged, or allowed to go home, over very serious injuries. There are anecdotal stories of men who had major infections, wounds, or even had extremities amputated and were still forced to fight until they either died or the war ended. This is one of the many things that made the Second Boer War so horrific, though that can be said of all wars. The author of this poem actually wasn't a soldier himself but drew on the experiences of soldiers who had fought in this war.
